The signs

How to tell it is overdue

Something is growing in it

A seedling in a gutter means there is soil in there, and soil means years of composting leaf rather than months.

Water comes over the front

An overflowing gutter is a blocked one. The water should be leaving down the pipe, and if it is coming over the lip it is going somewhere it should not.

There is staining down the fascia

A dark streak below the gutter line marks a long term overflow point, and it tells you where the blockage is without anyone getting up there.

The downpipe is silent in heavy rain

A working downpipe is audible. One that stays quiet while water pours off the roof is blocked.

The roof above

Clearing the roof, not just the gutter

Clearing an Eltham gutter and leaving a roof covered in leaf and lichen means the gutter is filling again within a season.

The roof feeds the gutter

Whatever is sitting on the tiles ends up in the gutter at the next decent rain. On an Eltham roof with lichen rooted into the tile surface it is worse, because the growth holds moisture and breaks down the glaze underneath it.

Which is why the roof surface gets cleared in the same visit, and why a roof wash is worth considering where the growth has taken hold. Roof cleaning.
